TimePeriod: Patriarchal era, before Esau's descendants took Seir
Region: Mount Seir (later Edom) and its mountains
History: The Horites (also called Horim) were the earlier inhabitants of Seir. Chedorlaomer defeated them in Mount Seir in Genesis 14:6, and Genesis 36:20-30 gives the genealogy of Seir the Horite and his sons: Lotan, Shobal, Zibeon, Anah, Dishon, Ezer, and Dishan, the dukes of the Horites. Deuteronomy 2:12 and 2:22 record that the children of Esau destroyed the Horites and dwelt in their stead, just as Israel would later do in Canaan.
Culture: Their name is traditionally connected with cave-dwelling in Seir's mountains. They were organized under dukes, a clan structure that Esau's line inherited along with the land.
Religion: No Horite religion is described in the text.
BibleConnection: The Horites show the pattern Deuteronomy repeats: one people displacing another in the land, so that Edom's story mirrors Israel's own conquest.
